messages:
Laura (docs): Hey team — quick question. My docs PR preview CI is failing linkcheck + content lint. The API defaults page currently says 'Responses are cacheable by default' which a reviewer flagged as incorrect given runtime behavior. Can someone confirm the expected Cache-Control/ETag behavior so I can update the SDK snippet? CI preview: https://ci.redwood/preview/3221 :thinking_face:

Sam (runtime): Short answer: generation/completion responses are served with `Cache-Control: no-store` by default. Embeddings are the only endpoint that emits ETag/conditional responses, and caching there is opt-in (e.g., `?cache=true` or a server-side flag). Streaming endpoints don't set cache headers. Is that the line you hit?

Laura (docs): Yep, exact sentence: 'Responses are cacheable by default.' That's what triggered the reviewer and the linter. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/812

Michael (devex): For the SDK example, do we show setting headers explicitly to disable caching? e.g.:
```javascript
// explicitly prevent intermediary caching for generation results
await client.generate({
  model: "redwood/rw-1",
  input: "...",
  headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" }
});
```

Tara (sdk): Quick note — our high-level JS `generate` helper doesn't accept a `headers` param today; headers live on the lower-level `request` call. If docs show the high-level helper accepting headers we should either update the SDK or show a `fetch` example.

Sam (runtime): Confirming behavior again: runtime enforces `no-store` for generation endpoints. For embeddings: when cache opt-in is enabled we return `ETag` and support `If-None-Match` to return 304s for identical inputs. No other endpoints set cache headers by default. There are no current plans to change defaults.

Laura (docs): Thanks. Could you drop a one-sentence wording we should use in the docs? Also: any migration notes (older clients that assumed cacheable responses)?

Sam (runtime): Suggested wording: "By default, generation responses include `Cache-Control: no-store`. Embeddings may be cached only when the embeddings cache opt-in is enabled; in that scenario responses include an `ETag` to support conditional requests." Migration: not breaking — older clients that cached responses may see fewer cached hits; recommend invalidating cached responses if they relied on stale behavior. I'll open a runtime note and link it here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1290

Michael (devex): I'll open a tiny SDK PR to add an example helper or document how to pass headers. @Tara can you review once it's up?

Tara (sdk): Yep, will review. Laura — you can update the docs line to Sam's suggested wording and add a short callout beneath the paragraph: "If you need caching for embeddings, see the embeddings cache opt-in and ETag section (link)." Once we have the SDK PR number we can link it so the example matches the code.

Laura (docs): Great — I'll update the line now and push. Will re-run preview. Thanks all :pray:

ci-bot: Build queued for preview #3221 — waiting on updated commit.
file_notes: Docs PR coordination thread about cache headers, CI preview blocking wording, SDK example mismatch; requests runtime wording and SDK follow-up.
